hypothesis: The linked SMP image rejects tampered contracts and expired deadlines and completes its scheduler interrupt and shared-lock cases under an instruction model.
conclusion: Host-only; the image check no longer exists, so the image has no host check.
narrative: Host-only result from a host check that has since been removed. The check snapshotted the repository dependencies and the pinned FreeRTOS inputs, built outside the repository and refused an existing evidence directory. It checked contract tampering, deadline refusal, watchdog-source refusal and per-core MMIO boundaries under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, inspected ELF segments and reserved symbols, and executed the linked scheduler interrupt calls for all eight destinations. Linked shared-lock checks covered primary and secondary completion, a missing peer and a held lock with deadline expiry. The instruction model did not reproduce physical inter-core contention. Evidence directory: ~/.cache/sunstoneos/evidence/a733-smp-image-20261016. The first configure needed the available Make generator and explicit linker propagation into compiler checks; linking then needed the runtime memmove, task-delete configuration and vector-table alias; those failures and the corrected commands remain in the evidence directory. The continuation's corrected EL3 reset constants changed only its assembly object, build identity and final link. The image manifest records executed and final artifact identities separately.

hypothesis: The AArch32 launcher and its host adapter handle admission and every refusal without touching a board.
conclusion: Launcher admission and refusal cases pass on the host; the host adapter checks no longer exist.
narrative: The launcher instruction check executed the linked AArch32 bytes with modeled registers and counter reads (admission, contract mismatch, ignored register writes, counter rollback, overflow, elapsed-time refusal). The host check (since removed) used a fake transport and a private SQLite queue to cover every request failure point, corrupt readback, changed claims and missing prerequisites; it verified one execution request and an unobserved scheduler result after ROM observation. The 2,036-byte launcher passed 28 instruction cases and its host adapter 41 protocol cases; evidence in ~/.cache/sunstoneos/evidence/a733-smp-launch-20261016. Focused host checks also covered ownership retention when evidence flushing or quarantine fails, durable backup flushes, source-identical evidence after integration and failure retention. The 2,220-byte launcher and refusal adapter (evidence ~/.cache/sunstoneos/evidence/a733-smp-refusal-20261016) passed sixteen focused instruction cases (caller-state restoration, ARM and Thumb returns, pre-mutation refusals, unsafe-context parking, the first-write boundary; selected with --focus-refusal) and seventeen focused host cases (fresh refusal reports, failure stopping, SRAM restoration, obsolete-layout refusal, upload changes after admission). Six further host cases covered source growth and replacement before and after sealing, replacement of restoration backups and descriptor inheritance by a child process (freeze-results.json in the refusal evidence directory). The reset, deadline and scheduler evidence was reused; the 2,220-byte launcher received a native compile and link. No physical request occurred. The checks do not model oscillators, interconnect stalls, warm reset completion, AArch64 entry or physical scheduling.
